name: Nahath
overview: Nahath was a male Levite who served as an overseer of the consecrated things under Conaniah, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:13. His role highlights a position of responsibility within the Levitical duties related to sacred items. There are no additional notes on his life or ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Nahath means 'descent' or possibly 'rest' in Hebrew. It is a proper name but was not given directly by God according to the biblical record in 2 Chronicles 31:13. This meaning may reflect a familial or tribal heritage but does not carry a specific divine title.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Nahath as a descendant of Levi, indicating his tribal lineage. Beyond this, no other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Nahath's significance lies in his role as an overseer of consecrated things, which underscores the importance of faithful service and stewardship within the Levitical priesthood. His mention in 2 Chronicles 31:13 connects him to the reforms and temple service during the time of King Hezekiah, reflecting a commitment to proper worship and dedication to God’s house. Though a minor figure, Nahath exemplifies the faithful administration of God’s sacred duties in the Old Testament.
